w_weather: a fog that smelled of apples
w_oddity: a cat asleep on a cannon
a three-legged stool that had been in the family for centuries
a map drawn on a bun

work.text: {a} stamped forty forms in {place} and found, to their surprise, that one of them was a love letter.
{a} reorganised the filing at {place} and lost, then found, then lost again, the whole of last Tuesday.
In {place}, {a} balanced a ledger that had not balanced in a decade, and wept a little.
{a} drafted a decree in {place} on the subject of pigeons. It was, said everyone, long overdue.
{a} drilled the recruits at {place}: left, right, left, spear, shield.
{a} walked the wall of {place} at dusk, as they did every night, and counted the stars to be sure none were missing.
At {place}, {a} showed a nervous recruit how to hold a shield, and how to hold their nerve.
{a} oiled a spear in {place} and told the story of the time the spear had won an argument.
{a} worked the bellows at {place} till the sparks flew like fireflies.
The anvil at {place} rang all afternoon under {a}'s hammer, a good, steady, hopeful sound.
{a} quenched a blade in {place}, and the hiss was like a small contented dragon.
{a} mended a cartwheel for a stranger in {place}, and refused payment, then accepted a pie.
{a} tested a new edge on a bale of straw at {place}, and the straw agreed with them.
At {place}, {a} balanced a sword on one finger, nodded, and set it by for a customer who would be very lucky.
{a} polished a spear in {place} until it showed their own, very concentrated, face.
{a} hammered out a dent in a breastplate at {place}, whistling.
At {place}, {a} fitted a helmet to a very small recruit with a very large head.
{a} riveted a pauldron in {place} and said it would stop a dragon, or at least a bad-tempered goose.
{a} set a flask to boil at {place}, and a small, pink cloud of something promising rose from it.
At {place}, {a} labelled a bottle “probably fine” and put it on the high shelf.
{a}'s latest tonic at {place} turned the cat blue. It purred. {a} wrote it down.
{a} stitched a banner in {place}, humming, with pins in their mouth.
At {place}, {a} took in a coat for a soldier who had been given less than a fair share of dinners.
{a} dyed a bolt of cloth in {place} a shade that was, the whole street agreed, *very* purple.
{a} set a small stone at {place}, with a jeweler's breath held and a jeweler's pride.
At {place}, {a} turned a gem to the light and found a rainbow inside it.
{a} polished a ring in {place} that had been waiting thirty years for its owner.
{a} planed a plank at {place}, and the curl of wood fell like a ribbon.
At {place}, {a} mended a stair, a shelf and a very rickety chair, in that order.
{a} measured twice and cut once in {place}, and was extremely smug about it.
{a} whittled a tiny knight at {place}, with an even tinier sword.
At {place}, {a} wound up a clockwork duck, which immediately escaped.
{a} painted the eyes on a puppet in {place}, and swore it winked.
{a} swept the step at {place} and put the good apples at the front.
At {place}, {a} tallied the day's takings on a slate and found them <w_crowd> short of a scandal.
{a} put out a sign at {place}: “Everything must go (except the cat).”
{a} shelved a stack of scrolls at {place} and found one that had not been read in a century.
At {place}, {a} shushed a child, then a bird, then, hopelessly, the wind.
{a} copied out a single line of an old prophecy at {place}, and sat very quiet.
{a} taught a class at {place} how to make a spark; one student made a small sun.
At {place}, {a} corrected a pupil's spell, gently, and rescued a curtain.
{a} lectured on the dangers of unsupervised conjuring at {place}, as a goose floated past.
{a} lit the candles at {place} one by one, and the room lit up with them.
At {place}, {a} blessed a soldier's boots, a baker's oven and a child's lost tooth.
{a} gave a short sermon at {place}: “Be kind. Be early. Bring snacks.”
{a} polished a mug at {place} and listened to a long, sad, wonderful story.
At {place}, {a} found <w_oddity> in the cellar, and decided not to ask.
{a} put the kettle on at {place}, and by the time it sang, all the regulars had arrived.
{a} stirred a pot at {place} that smelled like everybody's home.
At {place}, {a} tasted the stew, added salt, tasted again, and decided, finally, it was done.
{a} peeled a mountain of potatoes in {place}, and didn't mind.
{a} pulled a tray of loaves out at {place}, and the whole street leaned in to sniff.
At {place}, {a} scored a loaf and said a quiet word to it.
{a} burned the first batch at {place}, and sold it as “rustic”.
{a} wove a wreath at {place}, from whatever the frost had missed.
At {place}, {a} tucked a flower into a passing soldier's collar, without a word.
{a} tended the window-boxes of {place}, and talked to them, and was answered.
{a} tuned a lute at {place}, and a small crowd gathered to be disappointed, and then wasn't.
At {place}, {a} sang the ballad of the missing sock, and wept at the second verse.
{a} rhymed “dragon” with “wagon” at {place}, and held their head high.
{a} ran to {place} with a letter, a parcel and a very strong opinion about shoes.
At {place}, {a} dropped off a message, collected another, and was gone before the tea was poured.
{a} took a shortcut through {place} and found, to their dismay, that it was longer.
{a} hoed a row at {place} and talked to the beans.
At {place}, {a} watched the sky for rain and, for once, was pleased.
{a} milked a cow at {place}, with great delicacy, since the cow was in a mood.
{a} mended a net at {place}, and watched the water for a long while.
At {place}, {a} landed a great silver fish and apologised to it.
{a} hauled in a catch at {place}, and found a boot, a bottle and a very surprised crab.
{a} swung a pick at {place} and the rock gave up, grumbling, a seam of something bright.
At {place}, {a} lit a lamp, ducked a beam, and went down.
{a} tapped the wall at {place} and listened to the stone answer.
{a} loaded a cart at {place} with spices, thread and a small barrel of optimism.
At {place}, {a} haggled for an hour, won, and gave it all back for the pleasure of the argument.
{a} counted coins at {place} and found, as ever, one fewer than expected.
{a} brushed a horse at {place} that had very strong feelings about brushes.
At {place}, {a} shovelled, sighed and shovelled again, in the quiet dignity of the trade.
{a} fed an apple to a stubborn mule at {place}, and was forgiven for last week.
{a} practised a lunge at {place} until the dummy begged for mercy.
At {place}, {a} sharpened a blade, then stood very still, rehearsing a single perfect strike.
{a} threw a few knives at {place}, bored, and hit the middle every time.
At {place}, {a} watched the fighters spar, and made notes on what they were doing wrong.
{a} stood at the gate of {place} and let a cart bounce harmlessly off.
At {place}, {a} lifted a shield, set it down, lifted it again, with the patience of a mountain.
{a} rolled bandages at {place} and counted the beds.
At {place}, {a} brewed a bitter tea, held a paw, and sat watch till dawn.
{a} carried water round {place}, and a good word, and neither ran out.
At {place}, {a} tied a stranger's bootlace and told them they looked ready.
{a} hummed a few quiet notes at {place}, and the whole room stood a little straighter.
At {place}, {a} laid a paw on a nervous recruit's shoulder, and the shaking stopped.
{a} polished the black glass at {place}, humming a surprisingly pretty tune.
At {place}, {a} filed a report on the Heroes: “They do seem rather nice.”
{a} carried a mountain of scrolls through {place}, and sneezed on the important one.
{a} chanted in {place}, and the candles leaned away, embarrassed.
At {place}, {a} rehearsed the choir, and was a half-tone flat.
{a} stood a silent watch at {place}, in armour that creaked.
At {place}, {a} wrote a letter to their mother, and then thought better of the signature.
{a} paced {place}, glowering, and had a quiet word with a mirror.
{a} stood at a high window in {place}, and said nothing, for a very long time.

world.text: [WORLD] In {place}, <w_festival> breaks out, with no particular reason, and no objection.
[WORLD] A peddler with <w_oddity> arrives in {place}. The children follow, at a distance.
[WORLD] A bard in {place} sings the ballad of the season so far, and gets two verses wrong.
[WORLD] Candles are lit in the windows of {place}, one by one, for no reason that anyone will give.
[WORLD] <w_weather> over {region}. The roads are muddy. The mood is good.
[WORLD] A small, stubborn flower opens in {place}, where nothing grew yesterday.
[WORLD] A stranger in a grey cloak passes through {place} and is gone by morning.
[WORLD] The guild hall at {place} runs out of stamps. A crisis is averted by a baker.
[WORLD] A child in {place} declares that they will be the Hero. The nearest adult nods, gravely.
